title: Five early believers each receive a distinct duty
setting: Soon after the Church was organized on 6 April 1830, five men asked Joseph Smith to learn their duties. They were Oliver Cowdery, Hyrum Smith, Samuel H. Smith, Joseph Smith Sr., and Joseph Knight Sr. Joseph dictated five short revelations, apparently one after another. The official heading places them at Manchester, New York. The Joseph Smith Papers place the related meetings in Fayette Township and suggest they came before an 11 April meeting.
summary: These are five brief revelations gathered into one section. Oliver Cowdery is told he is under no condemnation but must beware of pride. He is to make his calling known to the Church and the world. Hyrum Smith is also under no condemnation and is called to exhort and strengthen the Church. His duty is to the Church forever, because of his family. Samuel H. Smith is called to exhort and strengthen the Church but not yet to preach to the world. Joseph Smith Sr. is called to exhort and strengthen the Church from then on. Joseph Knight Sr. is told to take up his cross and pray aloud in every setting. He is also told it is his duty to unite with the true church.

contextNote.title: A cross for the one not yet joined
contextNote.text: Four of the five men are told they are “under no condemnation,” but Joseph Knight Sr. is not. Verse 6 tells him instead to “take up your cross.” The cross is specific: praying aloud before the world, in his family, and among friends. Verse 7 adds that his duty is to unite with the true church. Knight had supported Joseph for years without joining, so open prayer and membership were public steps. In this passage, the “cross” is the cost of making private belief visible.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 23–26, “Seek for the Things of a Better World,” shows the Lord giving individual direction. Each man in verses 1–7 gets a slightly different calling. What does Samuel’s “not as yet” in verse 4 teach about personal timing?
reviewNote: Read all 7 verses. Official heading gives Manchester, April 1830, to five named men. JSP lists five documents (April 1830–A through E); only the introduction to April 1830–A [D&C 23:1–2] was loaded. It dates them between 6 and 11 April and places the meetings in Fayette Township, with a footnote suggesting Palmyra. receivedAt follows the official heading. The claim that Knight had not yet joined rests on verse 7; JSP text loaded did not discuss his baptism, which is generally dated to June 1830 at Colesville. Fact-check 2026-10-12: summary no longer says Hyrum’s calling came because of his family; verse 3 ties his lifelong duty to the Church to his family.
